newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp raises stake in Canadian funeral firm.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp raises stake in Canadian funeral firm.

text.p: Funeral home giant Service Corp. International said Monday it agreed to nearly double its investment in Canada's Arbor Memorial Services Inc., buying the stake for $69 million from archrival Loewen Group Inc.
Following the transaction, Houston-based SCI will own 59 percent of Arbor's outstanding shares. The deal represents the latest move by Service Corp. (SCI) in an aggressive acquisition programme.
"This investment strengthens our positive relationship with Arbor, and SCI may continue to increase its investment in Arbor," SCI Chairman Robert Waltrip said in a news release.
SCI is the world's largest funeral services company, operating 3,012 funeral homes, 365 cemeteries and 156 crematoria.
In a telephone interview, SCI President William Heiligbrodt said the transaction will immediately add to earnings. He declined to be more specific.
Heiligbrodt said that while there are no current plans to take over the rest of Arbor, "we think this is a company we ultimately would like to own."
Arbor operates 83 funeral homes, 44 cemeteries and 25 crematoria in Canada.

Vancouver, British Columbia-based Loewen offered little insight into the reason for the sale, saying only that it "does not believe that a minority interest in the company is the most effective use of its capital at this time.

Loewen, which earlier this year fought off a $2.9 billion hostile takeover by SCI, has been pressured in recent months by declining death rates and concerns about earnings growth. The company has been trying to increase sales of plots and monuments to people making plans in advance of their deaths -- so-called "pre-need" sales.
Loewen said it expects the transaction, which is subject to apporoval by Canadian regulators, to result in a one-time pretax gain of $26 million.
Service Corp. stock fell 6 cents to $32.06 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Loewen stock lost 25 cents to $33.55, also on NYSE.
